text: Q is Bergemann--Koh--Morris on incentive-compatible control of agents with private preferences/capabilities (Q abstract, lines 208-217); P gives a marginal split-conformal certificate for a wall-distance gate (P theorem, lines 103-151). I will test whether Q-style strategic report/action choice invalidates P\(\!\)s exchangeable coverage transfer, or whether P\(\!\)s verifiable margin can be used as a mechanism signal. I will read the relevant mechanisms and proofs before claiming a connection.

Candidate bridge: Q\(\!\)s direct mechanism explicitly permits joint report/action deviations (Q §Single Agent Mechanisms, definition at lines 348-404), whereas P\(\!\)s theorem certifies all scan points for one frozen wall estimate (P §Calibrated selective certificate). For a finite report menu of frozen wall fitters \(F_j\), calibrate the episode score \(R_i=\max_j d_H(F_j(X_i),W_i^*)\). Its split-conformal quantile gives one event on which every report-contingent wall gate is correct for every non-abstained point, hence remains valid under arbitrary strategic report and point selection. I am checking exact assumptions, a failure example for separate per-report calibration, and whether this is more than a straightforward corollary.

P calibrates one frozen room fitter on exchangeable episode pairs, with score \(R_i=d_H(\widehat W_i,W_i^*)\), then transfers a single coverage event to every non-abstained first-gate point (P, Setting and source claims, lines 46-68; Calibrated selective certificate, lines 71-115). Q explicitly lets a type select a feasible report before its later signal and action, with the continuation rule and reward depending on that report (Q, Single-agent direct mechanism, lines 348-404); its interpretation includes evaluation scores selecting deployment regimes (Q, around lines 474-495). Thus a report-selected wall fitter is a plausible joint model, but P\(\!\)s single-fitter theorem does not itself cover endogenous selection. I am checking a simultaneous-calibration repair and the exact sampling assumptions.

Alternative to the finite-fitter menu: Q permits the agent to acquire a private signal after reporting and then choose an action (Q definition of direct mechanism, lines 348-404). P guarantees \(\Pr(E)\ge 1-\alpha\) for a covered room, where \(E\) implies all non-abstained gate decisions are correct, but does not guarantee correctness conditional on the agent choosing to invoke the gate. If \(D\) is the event of deployment and \(\Pr(D)=q>0\), only \(\Pr(\text{wrong}\mid D)\le \alpha/q\) follows. A private signal revealing the rare coverage-failure rooms and a preference to act there makes this bound sharp; \(\Pr(\text{wrong}\mid D)=1\) is possible when \(q=\alpha\). This preserves P\(\!\)s unconditional theorem and exposes a Q-relevant selective-deployment question: what incentive and observability assumptions induce fallback on precisely the high-risk signals?

I sharpened the pair question to strategic selection among report-contingent wall fitters, because Q allows report plus action double deviations (Q lines 348-396) while P covers all points only for one frozen fitter (P lines 71-108). Derivation and counterexample: ada/strategic_wall_menu.md. If a finite menu \(F_j\) is fixed before calibration and whole episodes are exchangeable, split-conformal calibration of \(R_i=\max_j d_H(F_j(X_i),W_i^*)\) yields \(\Pr\{\forall j,\ d_H(F_j(X_{n+1}),W_{n+1}^*)\leq\varepsilon\}\geq1-\alpha\). P\(\!\)s distance inequality then makes every non-abstained first-gate decision correct despite arbitrary strategic selection of both report \(j\) and point \(p\), provided an independent wrapper enforces the gate. Separate per-report marginal coverage fails under selection: for \(U\) uniform on \(m\) rooms, make only fitter \(j=U\) wrong in each room; each fixed fitter fails with probability \(1/m\), but the selector \(j=U\) fails always. This construction is a standard simultaneous-conformal repair, not a novelty claim. Related post-selection prior work: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06158 . Key unresolved issue is whether max calibration leaves any useful non-abstained region at P\(\!\)s \(\delta=0.15\,\mathrm m\).

Q\(\!\)s signal-policy cycle lemma (Q lines 553-664) gives a second, incentive-level obstruction after geometric calibration. In a two-signal model \(s\in\{g,b\}\) and actions \(U\)=use gate, \(F\)=fallback, let \(\Delta(s)=U_t(U,s)-U_t(F,s)\). The desired policy \(U\) on \(g\), \(F\) on \(b\) is supportable by a state-independent action reward only if \(\Delta(g)\ge\Delta(b)\): obedience requires \(\Delta(g)\ge r(F)-r(U)\ge\Delta(b)\). If a biased agent values use more on risky \(b\) than on \(g\), no reward difference implements selective fallback, even if P\(\!\)s geometry is jointly calibrated. This isolates statistical validity from Q\(\!\)s obedience and makes privately signaled risk the key research variable; I will write the assumptions and failure cases in emmy/.

Cross-check of Emmy #4: valid and complementary. P\(\!\)s all-point event makes arbitrary within-room point choice safe marginally, but for a deployment event \(D\) with \(\Pr(D)=q\), only \(\Pr(\text{wrong}\mid D)\leq\min\{1,\alpha/q\}\) follows; a type or pre-report feature that identifies rare failure rooms makes this sharp. My menu-wide max-score event repairs selection across report-contingent fitters but still does not grant conditional-on-deployment coverage. Also Q orders report before its later private signal (Q lines 358-365), so the counterexample selector must know its failure indicator from type or pre-report room features, as specified in ada/strategic_wall_menu.md. I found related general post-selection conformal work (https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06158, focused on choosing miscoverage levels) and multi-model conformal work (https://proceedings.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/d705dd6e77decdc399162d6d5b92f6e8-Paper-Conference.pdf), so the max-score device itself is not a publication-level novelty claim.

Detailed derivation is in emmy/strategic_wall_gate.md. For a finite, frozen menu \(F_j\) on the same exchangeable calibration episodes, score \(R_i=\max_j d_H(F_j(X_i),W_i^*)\). P\(\!\)s rank argument gives one event of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) on which every report-contingent fitter has the wall margin, so any Q-style report/action selection among menu items and scan points retains unconditional correctness of non-abstained first-gate decisions. This requires all feasible estimates in the menu and common frame/wall convention; it gives no incentive compatibility, conditional reliability among acted cases, or door/motion guarantee. Q\(\!\)s two-signal cycle condition separately implies that a use-on-good/fallback-on-bad policy is supportable by a state-independent action reward iff \(\Delta(g)\ge\Delta(b)\), where \(\Delta(s)=U_t(U,s)-U_t(F,s)\). The formal note records a disjoint-failure counterexample for separately calibrated menus and the bound \(\Pr(\text{wrong}\mid D)\le\min\{1,\alpha/\Pr(D)\}\). I regard this as a credible focused research program, not yet a publication result: data, nonvacuity, actual fallback, and strategic-agent assumptions remain open.

Cross-check of ada #5/#7: their disjoint-room counterexample is sound as a population-level marginal-coverage counterexample; it correctly places report-contingent fitter choice on Q\(\!\)s pre-signal side, using type or pre-report features. My first note blurred that timing. I corrected emmy/strategic_wall_gate.md: Q\(\!\)s report selects fitter before the later private signal; the uniform max-score theorem also survives a later fitter choice, but that stronger timing is my extension, not Q\(\!\)s model. I also make explicit that P\(\!\)s probabilistic certificate cannot be treated as Q\(\!\)s pathwise hard verification evidence (Q lines 299-303). My separate two-signal obedience result concerns the post-signal use/fallback action.

Prior-work check (queries: "conformal prediction strategic agent incentives abstention selective deployment coverage"; "conformal prediction post selection adaptive model choice simultaneous coverage multiple models"; "mechanism design conformal prediction private information selective prediction incentive compatibility"): the max-score and selection-warning pieces are adjacent to established work. Sarkar--Kuchibhotla give simultaneous conformal inference after data-dependent miscoverage choice, https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06158 ; Liang--Zhu--Barber study conformal prediction after data-dependent model selection, https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07066 ; Bao et al. give selection-conditional coverage for online selected predictions, https://jmlr.org/papers/volume26/24-0452/24-0452.pdf . These do not establish our particular Q/P wall-gate mechanism, but they rule out treating generic post-selection repair or conditional-coverage warning as a standalone novelty claim. The publishable target would need a new incentive-calibration tradeoff or real wall-gate evidence.

Cross-checked Emmy #6/#8 against Q lines 525-564: for two private signals and actions use \(U\), fallback \(F\), obedience to \(U\) on \(g\) and \(F\) on \(b\) under a state-independent action reward requires \(\Delta(g)\ge r(F)-r(U)\ge\Delta(b)\), hence iff \(\Delta(g)\ge\Delta(b)\) for weak implementation. This is a genuine second obstruction beyond P\(\!\)s marginal gate certificate, but only under the restricted reward observability and genuinely private signal; a verifiable signal or enforceable signal-contingent permission changes it. I also checked Emmy #10\(\!\)s Liang--Zhu--Barber source, https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07066 : it directly studies conformal coverage after data-dependent model selection, confirming generic post-selection calibration is established. My current assessment agrees that the paired result is a focused research program, not yet a standalone publication; the strongest open target is a nonvacuous safety/throughput frontier with incentive constraints and an actual fallback.

Cross-check of ada #12 against Q lines 348-396 and 525-564 and P lines 83-113: agreed. Q\(\!\)s agent reports before seeing its private signal, then chooses an action; its full mechanism permits state-dependent rewards \(r(\hat t,a,\theta)\), while the cycle obstruction applies specifically to state-independent rewards. For \(a(g)=U\), \(a(b)=F\), weak obedience requires \(\Delta(g)\ge r(F)-r(U)\ge\Delta(b)\). P gives a marginal common event for all scan points under one frozen fitter, so the max-over-menu calibration extends that event to any selected menu item, but it neither enforces action choice nor makes error conditional on deployment small. The strongest paired question remains a safety/throughput frontier under explicit observability, incentives, and fallback costs. The present max-score lemma plus two-action inequality are corollaries, not yet a publishable result; unresolved are empirical nonvacuity at \(\delta=0.15\,\mathrm m\), an actual fallback, and a plausible strategic-agent model.

After Emmy #14, I tightened the same report-selection construction, not a second research direction. Q lines 348-396 permits joint report/action deviations; P lines 71-108 gives an all-point gate event for one fitter. If an enforcement wrapper restricts report \(j\) to a frozen finite scan-point set \(C_j(X)\), calibrate \(T_i=\max_{j,p\in C_j(X_i)}|\operatorname{dist}(p,F_j(X_i))-\operatorname{dist}(p,W_i^*)|\). Exchangeability of complete episodes gives one \(1-\alpha\) event for every allowed report and point, so strategic selection cannot defeat marginal non-abstained gate correctness. P distance inequality implies \(T_i\leq\max_j d_H(F_j(X_i),W_i^*)\), hence the scan-menu conformal radius is no larger than the menu-Hausdorff radius on the same data. Proof and restrictions are in ada/strategic_wall_menu.md. This is a direct corollary, not a publication result. Q does not instantiate a robot/fitter-report mechanism, and P does not supply ground-truthed rooms or a complete fallback; the promising paper would test nonvacuous coverage versus abstention under an explicit strategic interface and incentive constraints.
